newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia fears "domino effect" after Taleban gains.
newsitem.headline: Russia fears "domino effect" after Taleban gains.

text.p: Russia put its troops in Tajikistan on full alert on Monday and said their presence was necessary to prevent the spread of fundamentalist Islam to Central Asia following gains by the Taleban militia in Afghanistan.
"(Russian troops) are needed to avert a 'domino effect' throughout the whole Central Asian region," Igor Ivanov, first deputy foreign minister, told Itar-Tass news agency.

Afghanistan's purist Islamic Taleban militia seized a chunk of northern territory, including the town of Mazar-i-Sharif, from the troubled anti-Taleban alliance last week, sending a wave of panic through the country's ex-Soviet neighbours.

Russia put its 201st Motorised Infantry Division, stationed in Tajikistan, on a state of "full military readiness", a Russian military source told RIA news agency. The troops were ready to move at any time towards the Afghan border.

The former Soviet Union withdrew its last soldiers from Afghanistan in 1989, ending a decade of unsuccessful military intervention on behalf of a leftist government which cost the lives of thousands of its troops.
Russia, which is separated from Afghanistan by more than 1,000 km (600 miles) of Central Asian territory to the north, has about 20,000 troops stationed in Tajikistan.
They guard the ex-Soviet republic's remote border with Afghanistan and carry out peacekeeping duties in Tajikistan, itself torn apart by a four-year civil war.

A fragile peace secured in Tajikistan last December with the involvement of the United Nations and Russian and Iranian diplomats is often rattled by maverick armed bands and drug traders acting out of bases in Afghanistan.

Ivanov warned that any collapse in peace talks between the republic's secular government and its armed Islamic opposition could see "a wave of instability from Tajikistan bring down other Central Asian states."

The United Nations said in a statement from the Tajik capital Dushanbe on Monday that the two sides plan to sign in the Iranian capital Tehran in Wednesday a "protocol on guarantees" for implementing the stalled peace agreement.
Ivanov added that any flood of Afghan refugees to Tajikistan, which has tens of thousands of its own population displaced, threatened to bring the war with them.
Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov has warned the Taleban not to violate the borders of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), a loose grouping of 12 ex-Soviet republics.
"(Any infringement) will provoke very tough and effective actions from the CIS side," Interfax news agency quoted Primakov as saying on Sunday.
